title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 7-8
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 7 to 8 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अग्राह्यः शाश्वतः कृष्णो लोहिताक्षः प्रतर्दनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 7 to 8 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 7 to 8.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 7 to 8** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अग्राह्यः शाश्वतः कृष्णो लोहिताक्षः प्रतर्दनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अग्राह्यः शाश्वतः कृष्णो लोहिताक्षः प्रतर्दनः । प्रभूतस्त्रिककुब्धाम पवित्रं मङ्गलं परम् ॥** **ईशानः प्राणदः प्राणो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः । हिरण्यगर्भो भूगर्भो माधवो मधुसूदनः ॥**

Beyond the reach of the senses, eternal, Krishna, red-eyed is he. The destroyer of foes is that God of gods. The purest, the very form of auspiciousness, is he. He rules over all, gives life, and is life itself. The eldest and the best of all is that God of gods. Hiranyagarbha, Madhava and Madhusudana is that Supreme Self.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 7 to 8 mean?
faq.a: Beyond the reach of the senses, eternal, Krishna, red-eyed is he. The destroyer of foes is that God of gods. The purest, the very form of auspiciousness, is he. He rules over all, gives life, and is life itself. The eldest and the best of all is that God of gods. Hiranyagarbha, Madhava and Madhusudana is that Supreme Self.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
